# Senchabot Extensions: full reference

> Free, open source stream overlays and tools for Twitch and Kick: Chat Box, Emote Wall, Sub Sprout, Subathon Timer, Stream Alerts, Sub Goal, Counter, Event List, End Credits, Viewer Queue, Top Supporters, Lower Thirds, Task List, Featured Message, Emote Combo, Bits & Kicks Goal, Now Playing, Stream Frames, Stream Countdown, IRL HUD Overlay, Weather, Chat Poll, Raffle, OBS Bridge and Spin Wheel. Each one is set up on a web page at https://extensions.senchabot.com and runs from a URL. No login and nothing to install.

Short version with links only: https://extensions.senchabot.com/llms.txt

## About

- Made by Senchabot (https://senchabot.com), an open source, multi-platform community bot for Twitch, Discord, Kick and YouTube.
- Source code: https://github.com/senchabot-opensource/monorepo, folder apps/extensions, GPL-3.0 license.
- Not affiliated with, endorsed by or partnered with Twitch or Kick.
- Price: free. There is no paid plan, no premium account and no watermark on the overlays.
- No login: you never create an account or connect a Twitch or Kick account. You type a channel name and get a URL. On Twitch the widgets read chat like an anonymous viewer, on Kick they listen to the public chat feed. They can't post in chat, moderate or see private account data.
- Streaming apps: OBS Studio and other apps that support browser sources. The guides are written for OBS Studio.
- Languages: English, plus German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Portuguese and Turkish under /de, /es, /fr, /ja, /pt and /tr (for example https://extensions.senchabot.com/tr/setup/chat-widget). Overlay and tool URLs are the same in every language; add ?lang=de, es, fr, ja, pt or tr to one to show its text in that language.
- Settings live inside the widget URL. Nothing is saved to an account, and anyone with the URL opens the same widget.
- Old URLs keep working: parameter names, values and defaults are not changed by updates.
- Data sources: chat comes straight from Twitch and Kick, emotes from 7TV, BetterTTV and FrankerFaceZ, Twitch channel IDs from ivr.fi, and Kick channel info from kick.com.

## Widgets at a glance

| Widget | Kind | Setup page | URL used in OBS | Browser source size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Box | Overlay | /setup/chat-widget | /widgets/chat-widget | 400x600 |
| Emote Wall | Overlay | /setup/emote-wall | /widgets/emote-wall | 1920x1080 |
| Sub Sprout | Overlay | /setup/sub-growing-plant | /widgets/sub-sprout-widget | 800x600 |
| Stream Alerts | Overlay | /setup/stream-alerts | /widgets/stream-alerts | 800x450 |
| Sub Goal | Overlay | /setup/sub-goal | /widgets/goal | 800x260 |
| Event List | Overlay | /setup/event-list | /widgets/event-list | 420x520 |
| End Credits | Overlay | /setup/end-credits | /widgets/credits | 1920x1080 |
| Viewer Queue | Tool | /setup/viewer-queue | /widgets/queue | 440x600 |
| Top Supporters | Overlay | /setup/top-supporters | /widgets/leaderboard | 440x380 |
| Lower Thirds | Overlay | /setup/lower-thirds | /widgets/lower-third | 1920x1080 |
| Task List | Overlay | /setup/task-list | /widgets/tasks | 480x720 |
| Featured Message | Overlay | /setup/featured-message | /widgets/featured | 720x240 |
| Emote Combo | Overlay | /setup/emote-combo | /widgets/emote-combo | 600x400 |
| Bits & Kicks Goal | Overlay | /setup/bits-goal | /widgets/goal?type=bits | 800x260 |
| Now Playing | Overlay | /setup/now-playing | /widgets/now-playing | 640x160 |
| Counter | Overlay | /setup/counter | /widgets/counter (changed from chat with its own commands) | 800x260, or 440x400 stacked |
| Stream Frames | Overlay | /setup/stream-frames | /widgets/frame | 640x360, 360x640, 420x720 or 1920x1080 |
| IRL HUD Overlay | Overlay | /setup/irl-hud | /widgets/irl-hud | 1920x1080 |
| Weather | Overlay | /setup/weather | /widgets/weather | 1920x1080 |
| Subathon Timer | Tool | /setup/subathon-timer | /widgets/subathon (run from chat with !subathon) | 800x300 |
| Chat Poll | Tool | /setup/chat-poll | /widgets/poll (run from chat with !poll) | 640x560 |
| Raffle | Tool | /setup/raffle | /widgets/raffle-overlay (winner overlay) | 1920x1080 |
| OBS Bridge | Tool | /setup/obs-bridge | /tools/obs-bridge (tab or OBS dock, not a source) | none |
| Spin Wheel | Tool | /setup/spin-wheel | /widgets/spin-wheel (spun from chat with !spin) | 800x800 |

All eleven work with Twitch and Kick. Stream Frames reads no chat, so it needs no channel. Chat Box, Emote Wall, Sub Sprout, Subathon Timer, Stream Alerts, Sub Goal, Counter, Chat Poll and Spin Wheel take a Twitch and a Kick channel in the same URL. OBS Bridge listens to both chats at once. Raffle runs on one platform at a time.

## How to add a widget to OBS Studio

1. Open the widget's setup page, type the channel name or paste the channel's link (twitch.tv/senchabot becomes senchabot), adjust the settings and copy the URL. A Kick name typed with _ switches to its kick.com spelling with - when only that one is a channel.
2. In OBS, select the scene, click + in the Sources dock and pick Browser.
3. Name the source, paste the URL into the URL field and set Width and Height to the size in the table above.
4. Click OK and place the source in the scene.

Notes:
- The background is already transparent. No chroma key, filter or custom CSS is needed.
- Leave "Shutdown source when not visible" and "Refresh browser when scene becomes active" off. Both reload the page, and the widget forgets what it was showing (a Raffle winner drawn while the source is off never shows). Sub Sprout, Subathon Timer, Sub Goal and Chat Poll keep their plant, time, count or poll through a reload but can't see subs or votes while the source is off. Stream Alerts only shows what comes in while the source is running.
- To make Chat Box text bigger, change Font Size on the setup page instead of stretching the source.
- To change a widget later, copy a new URL from the setup page and paste it over the old one. Chat Box, Emote Wall, Sub Sprout, Subathon Timer, Stream Alerts, Sub Goal, Chat Poll and Stream Frames can load an existing URL: paste it into the Widget URL field on the setup page and all settings come back.
- If a widget looks empty: check that its URL has the channel name, not a link (twitch=senchabot), and that it is spelled right. Chat Box and Emote Wall stay empty until something happens in chat.

## Chat Box

Merges Twitch and Kick chat into one overlay.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/chat-widget?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL
- Demo with sample chat: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/chat-widget?mock=true
- Recommended size: 400x600 for a vertical column. For a horizontal bar, use the bar's length as width and one line of messages as height.
- Emotes: Twitch and Kick native emotes always show as images. 7TV channel and global emotes show in Twitch and Kick messages. BTTV and FFZ emotes show in Twitch messages only. On Kick messages 7TV uses the set linked to the channel's Kick account, or the Twitch set if only Twitch is linked on 7TV. If two emotes share a name, the channel emote wins, and the order between providers is 7TV, BTTV, FFZ.
- Hide Bots hides nightbot, streamelements, streamlabs, moobot, fossabot, wizebot, sery_bot, soundalerts, streamlootsbot, kofistreambot, pokemoncommunitygame, own3d, blerp, botrix, kickbot, kicklet and senchabot (Kick sends some of them with an "@" in front, which still matches), plus accounts with Twitch's Chat Bot badge or Kick's Bot badge.
- Hide Commands hides every message that starts with "!".
- Deleted messages and messages from users who get a timeout or ban are removed from the overlay.
- It only reads chat. It does not restream and can't post in chat.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel name | none |
| kick | Kick channel name | none |
| sevenTv | true, false | true |
| bttv | true, false | true |
| ffz | true, false | true |
| badges | true, false (broadcaster, moderator, VIP and subscriber badges) | true |
| fontSize | pixels (the setup page allows 8 to 72) | 18 |
| font | inter, roboto, nunito, mono (JetBrains Mono), serif (Source Serif 4), system | inter |
| layout | inline, stacked, card, compact | inline |
| animation | slide, smooth, pop, bounce, stagger, fade, typing, none | slide |
| orientation | vertical, horizontal | vertical |
| platformDisplay | icon, name, none (only used when both channels are set) | icon |
| platformAccent | true, false (purple stripe for Twitch, green for Kick) | false |
| background | true, false (semi-transparent black background) | false |
| bgOpacity | 0 to 1, used with background=true | 0.5 |
| itemBackground | true, false (a box behind each message) | false |
| chatBackground | true, false (one backdrop behind all messages) | false |
| boldUsernames | true, false | false |
| boldMessages | true, false | false |
| timestamp | true, false | false |
| duration | seconds a message stays (the setup page offers 10, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300) | 30 |
| keep | true keeps messages on screen, up to the last 100; overrides duration | false |
| hideBots | true, false | false |
| hideCommands | true, false | false |
| highlights | comma list of mention, reply, firstMessage, announcement, highlighted | none |
| mock | true plays sample chat | false |
| mockRate | sample messages per second, 0.1 to 50 | about 0.3 |

Highlights: mention and reply work on both platforms. firstMessage, announcement and highlighted (Highlight My Message) are Twitch only, because Kick doesn't send that info.

## Emote Wall

Shows emotes from chat on screen, anywhere on a full canvas.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/emote-wall?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL
- Demo with sample emotes: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/emote-wall?mock=true
- Recommended size: 1920x1080, placed above the gameplay.
- By default only messages made entirely of emotes count. With showAllEmotes=true, up to 5 emotes are also taken from normal text messages.
- 7TV: the emotes in the Twitch channel's active 7TV set, used in Kick chat too. It needs the Twitch channel in the URL.
- Modes: calm (pops up at a random spot, drifts and fades out), chaos (flies in from a random edge and vanishes between halfway and the far side), bounce (bounces off the edges and speeds up on every hit), glide (drifts down from the top of the screen, swaying side to side, and fades out near the bottom), spin (fades in at a random spot, spins around once or twice, then fades away), burst (appears, then pops into emote fragments and colored sparks before its time ends), random (every emote gets a random animation).

URL parameters (all optional; numbers out of range are clamped, invalid ones use the default):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel name | none |
| kick | Kick channel name | none |
| sevenTv | true, false | true |
| mode | calm, chaos, bounce, glide, spin, burst, random | calm |
| size | emote size in pixels, 32 to 256 | 112 |
| duration | seconds on screen, 2 to 30 | 5 |
| max | emotes on screen at once, 1 to 120 (oldest removed first) | 25 |
| subsOnly | true shows only emotes from subscribers, founders and the broadcaster | false |
| subDurationX2 | true keeps subscriber emotes on screen twice as long | false |
| showAllEmotes | true also uses emotes inside normal messages | false |
| hypeMode | true shows an emote only after 2 or more chatters send it within 15 seconds, then at most once every 15 seconds | false |
| spamBlock | true skips a chatter's emote messages beyond 3 in 10 seconds, and the same emote beyond 2 in 10 seconds | true |
| subEmotes | true shows only the channels' subscriber emotes | false |
| mock | true plays sample emotes | false |

## Sub Sprout

A plant that grows one stage with every new sub, resub or gifted sub on Twitch and Kick. On Kick every gifted sub counts as one stage.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/sub-sprout-widget?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL
- Demo with simulated subs: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/sub-sprout-widget?simulate=true
- Recommended size: 800x600.
- The broadcaster and moderators can type !grow in chat to grow the plant by one stage, or !grow reset to start it over.
- The plant is saved inside OBS. It survives reloads and carries over to the next stream. Picking another plant in the URL starts it over.
- When the plant is fully grown, the next sub starts it over according to the pick setting.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel name | none |
| kick | Kick channel name | none |
| variety | classic (10 stages), rose (10), sunflower (7), cactus (6), tulip (7), pine (5), lotus (7), lily (9), palm (10), vine (11) | classic |
| pick | fixed (same plant), cycle (next in the list), random; cycle and random never pick vine | fixed |
| water | off, rain, sparkle (plays when the plant grows; vine doesn't show it) | off |
| countfx | 0 hides the sub count badge (for example x5 for a 5-gift bundle) | shown |
| potlabel | 1 writes the stage on the pot, like 3/10 (vine doesn't show it) | hidden |
| simulate | true or 1 grows with simulated subs, doesn't read chat and doesn't save the plant; auto simulates until chat connects | off |
| channel, platform | older single-channel form (platform is twitch or kick); still read | none |

## Subathon Timer

A subathon countdown for Twitch and Kick. Subs, gifted subs, Bits (Twitch) and Kicks (Kick) add time, with separate values per platform; at zero the subathon is over.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/subathon?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL
- Demo with simulated subs: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/subathon?simulate=1
- Recommended size: 800x300. The overlay scales to any source size.
- The timer is saved in the browser source (OBS keeps it across reloads and restarts). While OBS is closed it keeps counting down, but subs in that time can't be seen.
- The health bar's 100% is the most time the timer has held, so the bar never goes over 100%.
- Once it reaches zero, subs no longer add time. A mod can bring it back with add or set, or start over with reset.
- On every heal, the heart (or the picked emoji or emote) flies from its spot to the bar's fill edge in the bar and thin styles.
- On Kick a sub is counted from SubscriptionEvent or ChannelSubscriptionEvent, whichever arrives, once per subscriber.

Chat commands for the broadcaster and moderators, on Twitch and Kick:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| !subathon start (or resume) | Starts or resumes the timer |
| !subathon pause (or stop) | Pauses the timer |
| !subathon add 10m | Adds time |
| !subathon remove 5m | Takes time away |
| !subathon set 2h | Sets the time left |
| !subathon reset | Starts over from the starting time |

Times can be written as 10m, 1h30m, 45s or 1:30:00; a plain number is minutes.

URL parameters (all optional, times in seconds):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel name | none |
| kick | Kick channel name | none |
| style | bar (health bar), thin (compact bar with embedded text), clock, ring | bar |
| color | hp (green to amber to red as time runs out), green, purple, red, gold, cyan, pink | hp |
| title | text shown with the timer, up to 32 characters; empty hides it | SUBATHON |
| icon | an emoji instead of the heart | none |
| iconUrl | a channel emote image instead of the heart, picked on the setup page | none |
| time | starting time | 3600 |
| cap | most time the timer can hold; 0 means no limit | 0 |
| tsub | Twitch: time per Tier 1 or Prime sub or resub | 60 |
| tgift | Twitch: time per gifted sub | 60 |
| bits | Twitch: time per 500 Bits; other amounts add their share | 60 |
| tiers | 0 counts Twitch Tier 2 and 3 subs and gifts like Tier 1 instead of 2 and 5 subs | 1 |
| ksub | Kick: time per sub or resub | 60 |
| kgift | Kick: time per gifted sub | 60 |
| kicks | Kick: time per 500 Kicks; other amounts add their share | 60 |
| shift | Threshold for dynamic rates; if > 0 and time left is above this, the tier 2 rates below apply | 0 |
| tsub2 | Tier 2 Twitch: time per Tier 1 or Prime sub or resub | 60 |
| tgift2 | Tier 2 Twitch: time per gifted sub | 60 |
| bits2 | Tier 2 Twitch: time per 500 Bits | 60 |
| ksub2 | Tier 2 Kick: time per sub or resub | 60 |
| kgift2 | Tier 2 Kick: time per gifted sub | 60 |
| kicks2 | Tier 2 Kick: time per 500 Kicks | 60 |
| autostart | 1 starts the timer when the overlay first loads instead of waiting for !subathon start | 0 |
| pct | 0 hides the percentage | 1 |
| pops | 0 hides the floating +1:00 added-time numbers | 1 |
| simulate | 1 plays simulated subs, doesn't read chat and doesn't save the timer | off |
| simspeed | clock speed for simulate, e.g. 60 for a minute per second | about 40 seconds for the whole bar |

## Stream Alerts

An alert box for Twitch and Kick. A new sub, gifted subs, Bits (Twitch), Kicks (Kick) or a raid each get an animated alert with an icon and a short sound.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/stream-alerts?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL&lang=en
- Demo with sample alerts: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/stream-alerts?simulate=1
- Recommended size: 800x450. The alert sits in the middle; the overlay scales to any source size.
- Themes: neon (an angular sci-fi banner with synth sounds) and celestial (a gold-line card under the stars with bell chimes).
- Alerts show one at a time, in the order they came in. A gift of many subs is one alert.
- Resub alerts show the months. A resub a viewer shares in chat (Twitch's resub message, Kick's chat celebration) gets an alert with the months and their message. Kick leaves the months out of subs on some channels.
- To hear the sound in OBS, turn on "Control audio via OBS" in the source and set it to Monitor and Output in Advanced Audio Properties.
- There are no follow or donation alerts: Twitch and Kick don't show follows to a page that isn't logged in, and neither has donations of its own.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel name | none |
| kick | Kick channel name | none |
| theme | neon, celestial | neon |
| color | platform (Twitch purple, Kick green), blue, purple, pink, red, gold, green | platform |
| lang | en, tr: the language of the alert text | the viewer's browser |
| sub, gift, bits, raid | 0 turns that alert off | on |
| hsub, hgift, hbits, hraid | custom heading for that alert, up to 24 characters | the language's default |
| mingift | smallest gift that shows, in subs | 1 |
| minbits | smallest cheer that shows, in Bits or Kicks | 1 |
| minraid | smallest raid that shows, in viewers; 0 also shows raids that come without a count | 0 |
| dur | seconds each alert stays on screen, 3 to 20 | 7 |
| vol | sound volume, 0 to 100; 0 is silent | 50 |
| msg | 0 hides the viewer's message with a resub, Bits or Kicks (links are always left out) | 1 |
| simulate | 1 plays silent sample alerts and doesn't read chat | off |
| simplatform | twitch or kick: simulate only that platform | both |

## Sub Goal

A sub goal bar for Twitch and Kick. Every new sub, resub and gifted sub from both chats adds to one count, and a trophy lands on the bar when the goal is reached.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/goal?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL&start=0&target=10
- Demo with simulated subs: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/goal?simulate=1
- Recommended size: 800x260. The rising +1s use the space above the bar; the overlay scales to any source size.
- A sub or resub adds 1, Prime and every tier alike. A gift adds 1 for each sub in it. On Twitch a resub counts when the viewer shares it in chat, on Kick when it renews. Twitch gift-sub continuations and Prime upgrades don't count, since that viewer is already subscribed.
- Neither platform shows a channel's sub count to a page that isn't logged in, so the count starts at the starting count in the URL and is saved inside OBS. It survives reloads and carries over to the next stream. A new starting count in the URL starts it over.
- The count keeps going past the goal; the bar stays full. Set `end` to `hide` and the completed goal hides itself after `endHold` seconds instead (0 hides it right away).
- When one sub or gift completes the goal, the trophy names who filled it.
- The broadcaster and mods fix the count from chat: !goal add 3, !goal remove 1 (add and remove take 1 when the number is left out), !goal set 25, !goal reset (back to the starting count).
- There is no follower goal: Twitch and Kick don't show follows to a page that isn't logged in.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel name | none |
| kick | Kick channel name | none |
| style | bar, thin (compact bar with embedded text) | bar |
| color | purple, green, red, gold, cyan, pink | purple |
| title | text shown above the bar, up to 32 characters; empty hides it | SUB GOAL |
| icon | an emoji instead of the star | none |
| iconUrl | a channel emote image instead of the star, picked on the setup page; it flies to the bar on every sub | none |
| start | starting count | 0 |
| start | starting count | 0 |
| target | the goal, 1 or more | 10 |
| end | stay (keep showing) or hide (hide the completed goal) | stay |
| endHold | seconds the completed goal stays up, 0 hides it right away | 0 |
| pops | 0 hides the rising +1 with the viewer's name | 1 |
| simulate | 1 plays simulated subs, doesn't read chat and doesn't save the count | off |
| simplatform | twitch or kick: simulate only that platform | both |

## Counter

A count of wins, losses, jump scares or anything else the streamer keeps score of. One browser source shows up to four counters, side by side or stacked, each with its own label, icon and chat command.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/counter?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL&c1=Wins&c1cmd=wins&c1icon=%F0%9F%8F%86
- Demo that counts on its own: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/counter?simulate=1&c1=Wins&c2=Losses&c3=Draws
- Recommended size: 800x260 side by side, the rising +1s use the space above the counters; 440x400 stacked. The overlay scales to any source size.
- Only the broadcaster and mods change the counts, from Twitch or Kick chat. Viewers typing a command change nothing.
- The commands, for a counter on !wins: !wins or !wins + adds 1, !wins +3 or !wins add 3 adds 3, !wins - or !wins -2 or !wins remove 2 takes off, !wins set 10 sets the count, !wins reset goes back to the starting count. A bare number (!wins 5) does nothing. A count never goes below 0.
- Every count is saved inside OBS per channel and command, so it survives reloads and carries over to the next stream. A new starting count in the URL starts that counter over; a new command starts from the starting count.
- An empty command, or one another counter in the URL already has, becomes count2, count3 and so on. The setup page warns when a command is also used by another widget.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel name | none |
| kick | Kick channel name | none |
| c1 to c4 | a counter's label, up to 24 characters, may be empty; each one present adds a counter | a Wins counter when none is given |
| c1cmd to c4cmd | the counter's command without the !: letters, digits and _, up to 20 | the label, lowercased |
| c1icon to c4icon | an emoji or a few characters next to the label | none |
| c1iconUrl to c4iconUrl | a channel emote image instead of the icon, picked on the setup page | none |
| c1start to c4start | starting count | 0 |
| layout | row (side by side) or stack (one under another) | row |
| pops | 0 hides the rising +1 and −1 | 1 |
| preset | see Presets | classic |
| color | purple, green, red, gold, cyan, pink (classic look only) | purple |
| simulate | 1 counts on its own, doesn't read chat and doesn't save the counts | off |

## Event List

A recent events list: the latest subs, resubs, gifted subs, Bits, Kicks and raids from Twitch and Kick in one list, each row marked with its platform, in the picked preset's look. Pick which events show, how many, the smallest cheers and raids that count, and whether rows fade. Mods clear it with !events clear. Browser source size 420x520.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/event-list?twitch=YOUR_TWITCH_CHANNEL&kick=YOUR_KICK_CHANNEL&lang=en
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/event-list?simulate=1
- Listens to Twitch IRC anonymously and Kick's Pusher WebSocket, both in one browser source, through the same event readers as Stream Alerts.
- A row per sub (months on a resub), gift (subs in it), Bits on Twitch or Kicks on Kick, and raid (viewers). Kick's second sub event fills in the months of the row already shown.
- Follows and donations aren't included: neither platform shows them to a page that isn't logged in.
- The list is saved in the browser source's `localStorage`, so a reload keeps it. Mods clear it with `!events clear`.
- URL parameters: `twitch`, `kick`, `sub`, `gift`, `bits`, `raid` (`0` hides that kind), `minbits` (fewest Bits or Kicks, 1 by default), `minraid` (fewest raid viewers), `rows` (3 to 10, 5 by default), `newest` (`top` | `bottom`), `fade` (seconds a row stays, 0 keeps it), `title` (above the list, none by default), `preset`, `color` (`platform` | `purple` | `green` | `red` | `gold` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `lang`, `simulate`.

## End Credits

Movie-style end credits: while the browser source runs, it collects everyone who subbed, gifted subs, cheered Bits or Kicks, raided, moderated or chatted on Twitch and Kick, and rolls them when its scene goes live in OBS. Mods roll it with !credits and clear it with !credits reset. Browser source size 1920x1080.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/credits?twitch=YOUR_TWITCH_CHANNEL&kick=YOUR_KICK_CHANNEL&title=Thanks%20for%20watching!&lang=en
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/credits?simulate=1
- Collects names while the browser source runs: subs, gifts, Bits and Kicks (biggest first), raiders, moderators and chatters from both chats. Bots and the broadcaster are left out of the chat list; a ban takes a viewer out.
- In OBS the roll starts when its scene goes live (OBS's `obsSourceActiveChanged` event) and stops when it leaves; in a browser tab it rolls at once. Keep "Shutdown source when not visible" off so it collects all stream.
- The names are saved in `localStorage`; after 12 hours without anything new the next stream starts empty. Mods use `!credits` (roll now), `!credits stop` and `!credits reset`.
- URL parameters: `twitch`, `kick`, `title` (first line), `outro` (last line, none by default), `subs`, `gifts`, `cheers`, `raids`, `mods`, `chatters` (`0` leaves that section out), `speed` (`slow` | `normal` | `fast`), `loop` (`0` rolls once), `preset`, `color` (`gold` | `purple` | `green` | `red` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `lang`, `simulate`.

## Viewer Queue

A viewer queue for playing with viewers: they type !join (or a join word you pick) in Twitch or Kick chat to get in line, with a note like their in-game name, and you or your mods call the next ones up with !next. Mods open, close, clear and remove with !queue. Browser source size 440x600.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/queue?twitch=YOUR_TWITCH_CHANNEL&kick=YOUR_KICK_CHANNEL&title=Viewer%20Queue&lang=en
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/queue?simulate=1
- Reads every message from both chats. Viewers join with the join word (`!join` by default) and an optional note, and leave with `!leave`; a ban takes them out.
- Mods: `!next` (calls up the group size) or `!next 3`, `!queue open`, `!queue close`, `!queue clear`, `!queue remove name`.
- Shows who's playing now, the numbered line and how many more are waiting. The queue is saved in `localStorage`.
- URL parameters: `twitch`, `kick`, `title`, `join` (the join word, `!join` by default), `subs` (`1` lets only subscribers join), `max` (most waiting, 0 for no limit), `rows` (names shown, 3 to 15), `group` (viewers per `!next`, 1 to 10), `preset`, `color` (`purple` | `green` | `red` | `gold` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `lang`, `simulate`.

## Top Supporters

A leaderboard: your top gifters or top Bits and Kicks givers from Twitch and Kick, or stream labels for the latest sub, gifted sub, cheer and raid. Totals keep counting until mods type !top reset. Browser source size 440x380.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/leaderboard?twitch=YOUR_TWITCH_CHANNEL&kick=YOUR_KICK_CHANNEL&board=gifts&title=Top%20Gifters&lang=en
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/leaderboard?simulate=1
- Counts gifted subs and Bits or Kicks per viewer from both chats (one Bit and one Kick count the same) and keeps the latest sub, gift, cheer and raid.
- Three boards: `gifts`, `cheers` and `latest`. The totals are saved in `localStorage` and keep counting from stream to stream until `!top reset`.
- URL parameters: `twitch`, `kick`, `board` (`gifts` | `cheers` | `latest`), `rows` (3 to 10 places), `title` (empty shows none), `preset`, `color` (`gold` | `purple` | `green` | `red` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `lang`, `simulate`.

## Lower Thirds

Animated lower thirds: a bar with your name or show title and up to 6 lines that take turns, in the picked preset's look, always up or on a timer, in any corner. No channel needed; with one, mods put up a line of their own with !lt and hide or show it. Browser source size 1920x1080.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/lower-third?title=YOUR_NAME&lines=Welcome%20to%20the%20stream!
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/lower-third?simulate=1
- A title and up to 6 lines that take turns every few seconds. With a hold time the bar slides in and out on a timer; 0 keeps it up.
- No channel needed. With one, the broadcaster and mods use `!lt <text>` (a line of their own), `!lt clear`, `!lt hide` and `!lt show`.
- URL parameters: `twitch`, `kick` (only for the chat commands), `title`, `lines` (joined with `|`, up to 6), `rotate` (seconds per line, 3 to 120), `hold` (seconds on screen, 0 keeps it up), `pause` (seconds away, 5 to 3600), `corner` (`bl` | `br` | `tl` | `tr`), `size` (50 to 200, percent), `preset`, `color` (`purple` | `green` | `red` | `gold` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `simulate`.

## Task List

A co-working task list for study and work streams: you and your viewers add tasks from Twitch or Kick chat with !task, tick them off with !done, change them with !edit and take them off with !remove. The broadcaster's tasks come first, a long list scrolls by itself, and mods clear it with !tasks clear. Browser source size 480x720.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/tasks?twitch=YOUR_TWITCH_CHANNEL&kick=YOUR_KICK_CHANNEL&title=Today%27s%20Tasks&lang=en
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/tasks?simulate=1
- Everyone changes only their own tasks: `!task <text>`, `!done` (or `!done 2`), `!edit <text>`, `!remove`. Mods: `!tasks cleardone`, `!tasks remove name`, `!tasks clear`.
- The broadcaster's tasks come first; the panel shows done and total tasks, and a long list scrolls down and back up. The list is saved in `localStorage`.
- URL parameters: `twitch`, `kick`, `title`, `max` (open tasks per viewer, 1 to 5), `done` (`0` takes finished tasks off at once), `speed` (scroll speed, 10 to 80 px a second), `preset`, `color` (`green` | `purple` | `red` | `gold` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `lang`, `simulate`.

## Featured Message

Puts a viewer's words on screen from Twitch or Kick chat: mods type !feature @name to show that viewer's last message with name color, badges and emotes (7TV, BTTV and FFZ too), and viewers ask with !q while mods run the line with !q next, !q skip, !q clear and !q off. Browser source size 720x240.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/featured?twitch=YOUR_TWITCH_CHANNEL&kick=YOUR_KICK_CHANNEL&lang=en
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/featured?simulate=1
- `!feature @name` (mods and the broadcaster) shows that viewer's last message from either chat, with name color, badges and emotes, 7TV, BTTV and FFZ included. `!feature` or `!feature off` hides it. The last message of up to 500 chatters is kept in memory; bots, replies and commands aren't.
- Viewers ask with `!q <question>` (up to 200 characters, one open question each; asking again replaces it). Mods: `!q next` shows the oldest, `!q skip` drops it, `!q clear` empties the line, `!q off` hides what's on screen.
- A ban, a timeout or a deleted message takes that viewer's message and questions off. The line and what's on screen are saved in `localStorage`.
- URL parameters: `twitch`, `kick`, `mode` (`both` | `feature` | `qa`), `hide` (seconds on screen, 0 keeps it up, up to 600), `waiting` (`0` hides the questions-waiting badge), `size` (50 to 150, percent), `preset`, `color` (`purple` | `green` | `red` | `gold` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `lang`, `simulate`.

## Emote Combo

When chatters post the same emote, a big combo counter shows the emote and how many chatters joined in, Twitch and Kick together, with 7TV, BTTV and FFZ emotes. It keeps the stream's best combo, which mods clear with !combo reset. Browser source size 600x400.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/emote-combo?twitch=YOUR_TWITCH_CHANNEL&kick=YOUR_KICK_CHANNEL&lang=en
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/emote-combo?simulate=1
- Each chatter counts once per combo, in any message with the emote. The combo shows from `min` chatters and keeps going while new chatters join within `window` seconds; then the final count stays up a moment and fades.
- Native Twitch and Kick emotes count per platform; 7TV, BTTV and FFZ emotes count by name, so the same 7TV emote in both chats makes one combo. Known bots don't count.
- The stream's best combo shows under the counter and is saved in `localStorage` for 12 hours. Mods clear it with `!combo reset`.
- URL parameters: `twitch`, `kick`, `window` (3 to 30 seconds), `min` (2 to 20 chatters), `size` (50 to 150, percent), `best` (`0` hides the best combo), `sevenTv`, `bttv`, `ffz` (`0` | `1`, which emote sets count; 7TV is on by default), `preset`, `color` (`gold` | `purple` | `green` | `red` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `lang`, `simulate`.

## Bits & Kicks Goal

A goal bar that every Twitch Bits cheer and Kick Kicks gift fills, 1:1, with a trophy when the target lands. It is the Sub Goal overlay with type=bits, with its own count and its own !bitsgoal command, so it runs beside a Sub Goal. Browser source size 800x260.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/goal?twitch=YOUR_TWITCH_CHANNEL&kick=YOUR_KICK_CHANNEL&type=bits
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/goal?simulate=1&type=bits
- The Sub Goal overlay with `type=bits`: Bits and Kicks add their amount 1:1 (both are about a US cent each); subs, gift subs and raids add nothing. Pops show the amount, and the trophy names whoever crossed the target.
- Its own count, saved in `localStorage` apart from the Sub Goal's, and its own command: `!bitsgoal`, with the same actions as the Sub Goal's `!goal`. A Sub Goal and a Bits & Kicks Goal run side by side on the same channels.
- URL parameters: the Sub Goal's, plus `type` (`bits`). The target starts at 1000 and the title at BITS & KICKS GOAL.

## Now Playing

Shows the song the streamer is listening to, with its cover art, title and artist, from ListenBrainz (Spotify connects there) or Last.fm. It reads no chat, so it works the same for Twitch and Kick streamers. Browser source size 640x160.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/now-playing?user=YOUR_LISTENBRAINZ_USERNAME&lang=en
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/now-playing?demo=1
- `source=listenbrainz` (the default) asks ListenBrainz's public playing-now API, which needs no key. Connect Spotify in ListenBrainz, or use any scrobbler that sends playing-now. Covers come from the Cover Art Archive when the song has a release ID.
- `source=lastfm` asks Last.fm for the recent tracks, which update almost at once. It needs a Last.fm API key built into the site (`VITE_LASTFM_API_KEY` at build time); without one, the setup page offers ListenBrainz only.
- The overlay asks every 12 seconds and backs off while a service is busy. When the music stops, the card dims, then slides out after `hide` seconds.
- URL parameters: `source` (`listenbrainz` | `lastfm`), `user`, `layout` (`card` | `pill`), `art` (`0` hides the cover), `album` (`0` hides the album line), `hide` (seconds before it slides out when nothing plays, 0 keeps it up dimmed, up to 60), `preset`, `color` (`green` | `purple` | `red` | `gold` | `cyan` | `pink`, classic only), `lang`, `demo`.

## Stream Frames

Ready-made frames for a webcam, a chat or the whole stream. The frame is drawn in the picked preset's look, with its own shape, ornaments and small animations: horns, spiked plates and rising sparks in Ancient, glowing teal gems in Rift, grass blocks and flickering torches in Blocks. The label sits in a tab on top of the camera and chat frames, and on a plate at the bottom of the screen frame. The middle is transparent, so the webcam or Chat Box under it shows through. It reads no chat and needs no channel.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/frame?piece=camera&preset=ancient&label=CHANNEL
- Demo with every piece on one canvas: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/frame?demo=1&preset=ancient
- Guide: https://extensions.senchabot.com/guides/stream-frames
- Recommended size: 640x360 for camera, 360x640 for a portrait camera (pick Portrait under Orientation, written as `orientation=portrait`), 420x720 for chat, 1920x1080 for screen. The frame is drawn for whatever size the source has, so a square webcam works too.
- In OBS, put the frame source above the webcam or Chat Box in the sources list. The opening is a little smaller than the frame's outer edge: in a 640x360 camera frame, a 590x296 webcam (a 16:9 camera cropped evenly at the top and bottom), centered on the frame, fills it without showing around the frame; in a 360x640 portrait camera frame, a 306x572 webcam (a 9:16 camera cropped evenly at the sides); in a 420x720 chat frame, a 370x660 Chat Box. Both scale with the frame.
- The drawings are original, with no game logos or art.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| piece | camera, chat, screen | camera |
| preset | rift, realm, flower, ancient, agent, defuse, blocks, pizza, storm, boost, airdrop, conquest, operator, banner, glitch | classic |
| color | purple, green, red, gold, cyan, pink (classic only) | purple |
| label | text in the top tab (camera, chat) or on the bottom plate (screen), up to 32 characters; empty leaves it off | none |
| motion | 0 turns the animations off | 1 |
| demo | 1 draws a stand-in webcam or chat; without piece it shows every piece on one canvas | off |

## Stream Countdown

A countdown for the parts of a stream where nothing is happening yet: the minutes before going live, a break in the middle, and the last minutes before signing off. The purpose (starting, break, ending, pomodoro) picks the default headline and icon, or set your own headline, note, end message and a custom icon per scene (an emoji, a few characters, or one of the channels' subscriber emotes from the setup page picker). It counts down a length, or aims at a time of day like 21:00 read from the clock of the computer running OBS, which means the source can be added hours ahead; a time that has already passed today aims at tomorrow. The clock starts when the browser source loads, so ticking "Refresh browser when scene becomes active" in OBS starts it over on every switch to that scene. At zero it shows a message (hides itself after `doneHold` seconds, 10 by default), holds 00:00, or hides itself. It needs no channel; with one, the broadcaster and mods change it from chat with !countdown.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/countdown?scene=starting&time=600
- Counting down to a time of day: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/countdown?scene=starting&at=21:00
- Demo: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/countdown?simulate=1
- Guide: https://extensions.senchabot.com/guides/stream-countdown
- Recommended size: 1920x1080, so the clock lands in the middle of the scene. It is drawn for whatever size the source has.
- Chat commands for the broadcaster and mods, on both platforms: `!countdown {scene} [duration] [headline] [| note]` (defaults to 10m, e.g. `!countdown break 5m Lunch | Back soon`), `!countdown add 5m`, `!countdown remove 2m`, `!countdown set 10m`, `!countdown pause`, `!countdown start`, `!countdown reset`, `!countdown cancel` (stops and hides it until the next command), `!countdown title <headline>`, `!countdown note <note>`. Durations are written as 5m, 90s, 1h30m, 5:00 or a bare number of minutes.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel, only for the !countdown commands | none |
| kick | Kick channel, only for the !countdown commands | none |
| scene | starting, break, ending, pomodoro | starting |
| time | seconds to count down, 1 to 86400 | 600 |
| at | a 24-hour time of day like 21:00 to count down to; replaces time | none |
| title | headline above the clock, up to 32 characters | the scene's wording |
| done | headline at zero, up to 32 characters | the scene's wording |
| doneHold | seconds the headline at zero stays up, 0 keeps it up | 10 |
| iconStarting | an emoji or a few characters instead of the starting icon | the scene's icon |
| iconBreak | an emoji or a few characters instead of the break icon | the scene's icon |
| iconEnding | an emoji or a few characters instead of the ending icon | the scene's icon |
| iconPomodoro | an emoji or a few characters instead of the pomodoro icon | the scene's icon |
| iconUrlStarting | a channel emote image instead of the starting icon, picked on the setup page | none |
| iconUrlBreak | a channel emote image instead of the break icon, picked on the setup page | none |
| iconUrlEnding | a channel emote image instead of the ending icon, picked on the setup page | none |
| iconUrlPomodoro | a channel emote image instead of the pomodoro icon, picked on the setup page | none |
| note | a line under the clock, up to 64 characters | none |
| end | text (a message at zero), hold (stay at 00:00), hide (nothing on screen) | text |
| look | card (a panel behind the clock), plain (text on the scene) | card |
| preset | rift, realm, flower, ancient, agent, defuse, blocks, pizza, storm, boost, airdrop, conquest, operator, banner, glitch | classic |
| color | purple, green, red, gold, cyan, pink (classic only) | purple |
| bar | 0 hides the bar that empties under the clock | 1 |
| motion | 0 turns the animations off | 1 |
| lang | en, tr (the wording of the scene) | the browser's language |
| simulate | 1 runs a fast countdown that starts over | off |

## IRL HUD Overlay

A game-style HUD for Twitch and Kick, made for IRL streams. Subs, gifted subs, Bits (Twitch), Kicks (Kick) and raids add the dollar amounts the streamer sets, with separate values per platform, and the cash counter rolls up to the new amount. Above it runs the time of day, in a picked time zone for OBS running on a cloud server or a computer at home. A mini-map shows an arrow walking streets or paths, turning at the corners, with the map turning under it so the arrow always points ahead. It draws a made-up city (Urban) or park (Park), picked by the channel name, or the real streets, paths, buildings, parks and water within about 350 m of a place the streamer saves (Real Place, starting at the first saved place), from OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors) loaded once per place from the Overpass API and kept in the browser source for 14 days; a radar sweep turns on the mini-map while it loads. On a real place the walk prefers footpaths and stays near the place. The setup page finds places with OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search, or takes pasted coordinates; each saved place has a one-word name mods switch to from chat.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/irl-hud?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL
- Demo with simulated subs: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/irl-hud?simulate=1
- Recommended size: 1920x1080, the whole scene. The money and the mini-map each sit in a picked corner and are sized for the source's short side, so a vertical canvas works too.
- The cash is saved in the browser source (OBS keeps it across reloads and restarts). Subs while OBS is closed can't be seen.
- A new starting amount in the URL starts the counter over from it; until then the money earned is kept.
- Bits and Kicks values are per 100, raids per viewer they bring. Twitch Tier 2 and 3 subs can count as 2 and 5 subs.

Chat commands for the broadcaster and moderators, on Twitch and Kick:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| !hud cash +500 (or !hud cash add 500) | Adds cash |
| !hud cash -200 (or !hud cash remove 200) | Takes cash away, down to a debt shown in red |
| !hud cash 10000 (or !hud cash set 10000) | Sets the cash |
| !hud cash reset | Goes back to the starting cash |

`!hud money` works the same as `!hud cash`. Every command also works in short, with `!h` in place of `!hud`: `!h cash +500`, `!h map park1`, `!h walk`. A plain `!h map`, `!h cash` (or money) and `!h time` (or clock) hide that part of the HUD, and the same command shows it again; the choice is saved in OBS. `!h weather` does the same for the Weather overlay when its URL has the channel.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| !hud map park1 | Switches the mini-map to the saved place named park1 |
| !hud map urban / !hud map park | Switches to the made-up city or park |
| !hud map reset | Goes back to the mini-map set in the URL |

The chosen mini-map is saved in the browser source until the URL's starting map changes.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| !hud walk / !hud run / !hud stay (or stop) | Starts the mini-map arrow walking or running, or stops it |
| !hud indoor (or inside) | Urban and Park maps only: takes the arrow into the building nearest it, where it walks within the walls while the map zooms in and dims the rest; the made-up park gets a stand-in building. A real place stays outdoors, and switching to one leaves the building |
| !hud outdoor (or outside) | Walks the arrow back out to the nearest street |
| !hud buy water | Buys the market item named water: its price comes off the cash |
| !hud buy water 3 | Buys three of it |

Market items and prices are set on the setup page. Without enough cash nothing is bought and the price shows with a cross.

Amounts can be written as 500, 1,500, $1500, 2.5k or 1m.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel | none |
| kick | Kick channel | none |
| style | retro (green $00000350 under a grey clock, round mini-map), modern (white $1,250, rounded square mini-map) | retro |
| corner | tr, tl, br, bl: where the cash and clock sit | tr |
| size | 50 to 200, percent | 100 |
| start | starting cash, 0 to 999999999 | 0 |
| tsub, tgift | dollars per Twitch sub (Tier 1 and Prime) and per gifted sub | 100 |
| bits | dollars per 100 Bits | 25 |
| traid | dollars per viewer a Twitch raid brings | 10 |
| ksub, kgift | dollars per Kick sub and per gifted sub | 100 |
| kicks | dollars per 100 Kicks | 25 |
| kraid | dollars per viewer a Kick raid (host) brings | 10 |
| tiers | 0 counts Twitch Tier 2 and 3 subs as one sub | 1 |
| clock | 0 hides the clock | 1 |
| h12 | 1 shows a 12-hour clock | 0 |
| tz | an IANA time zone like Europe/Istanbul for the clock | the OBS computer's |
| radar | 0 hides the mini-map | 1 |
| radarCorner | tr, tl, br, bl: where the mini-map sits | bl |
| map | urban, park, real: what the mini-map draws | urban |
| places | saved places as name:lat,lon joined by ; (one-word names, up to 10, not urban, park or reset); older URLs with lat and lon read as one place named place1 | none |
| move | walk, run, stay: how the mini-map arrow moves at the start | walk |
| items | market items as name:price joined by ; (up to 20, prices from 1 to 1000000) | none |
| pops | 0 hides the +$100 that floats up with the viewer's name | 1 |
| simulate | 1 plays simulated subs, doesn't read chat and doesn't save | off |

## Weather

Live weather for any place the streamer picks: an icon, the temperature and the weather in words (Sunny, Light rain, Thunderstorm and so on), with wind and humidity, and a forecast row for the coming hours (every third hour on the clock) or for today and the next three days with highs and lows. It comes as a card or a one-line pill, on a dark, light or no panel. The data is MET Norway's Locationforecast (the Norwegian Meteorological Institute), free under CC BY 4.0 with no account or API key; the overlay credits MET Norway in small print. The browser source asks for a new forecast when MET's Expires header says, about every half hour, and saves it in the browser source, so a reload shows the weather at once. It reads no chat and needs no channel. The setup page finds the place with OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search or takes pasted coordinates; the overlay shows only the name the streamer gives the place, never the coordinates.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/weather?lat=41.0082&lon=28.9784&place=Istanbul&lang=en
- Demo with sample weather: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/weather?demo=1
- It needs no channel. With twitch and/or kick in the URL, the broadcaster and mods hide it and show it again with !h weather (or !hud weather) in either chat; viewers typing it change nothing.
- Recommended size: 1920x1080, the whole scene. The weather sits in a picked corner and is sized for the source's short side, so a vertical canvas works too. Its default corner, top left, stays clear of the IRL HUD Overlay's.

URL parameters:

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch, kick | optional channels, only for !h weather | none |
| lat, lon | the place, with at most 4 decimals; nothing shows without them | none |
| place | the name shown with the weather, up to 40 characters | none |
| units | metric (°C, km/h), imperial (°F, mph) | metric |
| layout | card, pill (one line, no forecast) | card |
| theme | dark, light, clear (no panel, white text with a shadow) | dark |
| corner | tr, tl, br, bl | tl |
| size | 50 to 200, percent | 100 |
| details | 0 hides wind and humidity | 1 |
| forecast | hours, days, off | hours |
| h12 | 1 shows forecast hours as 3 PM instead of 15:00 | 0 |
| tz | an IANA time zone like Europe/Istanbul for the forecast's hours and days | the OBS computer's |
| lang | en, de, es, fr, ja, pt, tr: the language of the weather words and weekdays | written by the setup page |
| demo | 1 shows sample weather and doesn't ask MET | off |

## Chat Poll

A chat poll for Twitch and Kick. The broadcaster and mods put a poll up from chat, viewers vote by typing a number, and votes from both chats go into one result with live bars, a countdown and the winner at the end. Twitch's own polls can't be read without logging in, so this poll takes votes from chat, the same way on both platforms.

- Widget URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/poll?twitch=CHANNEL&kick=CHANNEL&lang=en
- Demo with simulated voters: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/poll?simulate=1
- Guide: https://extensions.senchabot.com/guides/chat-poll
- Recommended size: 640x560, room for a poll with 6 options. The poll sits at the top or bottom and grows with its options; the overlay scales to any source size.
- Chat commands for the broadcaster and mods: !poll Question | A | B (2 to 6 options), !poll 2m Question | A | B (its own length: 90s, 2m, 1:30), !poll Question? (a Yes/No poll), !poll start (the ready-made poll saved in the URL), !poll extend 30s, !poll end (results now), !poll cancel (off the screen).
- Viewers vote with the whole message: 2, !2, !vote 2 or an option's own text, in any case, with or without accents or Turkish letters. A message with more in it ("2 please", 4Head) isn't a vote. Twitch's /vote command is for Twitch's own polls, so viewers should type the number.
- One vote per Twitch or Kick account. With vote changing on (default), a new vote moves it; a vote for an option that doesn't exist keeps the old one. A timeout or ban while the poll is open takes the account's vote off.
- Viewers watch a few seconds behind chat, so votes keep counting for the stream delay after the timer ends, then the winner or a tie shows.
- The poll and its votes are saved inside OBS and survive a reload. The timer keeps running while OBS is closed.

URL parameters (all optional):

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel name | none |
| kick | Kick channel name | none |
| q | question of the ready-made poll, up to 80 characters | none |
| o | options of the ready-made poll, 2 to 6, split with a pipe, up to 30 characters each | none |
| dur | seconds a poll takes votes, up to 3600; 0 keeps it open until !poll end | 60 |
| delay | seconds late votes still count after the timer ends, 0 to 30 | 5 |
| hold | seconds the results stay up, up to 600; 0 keeps them until the next poll | 30 |
| subs | 1 lets only subscribers (sub or founder badge) and the broadcaster vote | 0 |
| subx | 2 or 3: a subscriber's vote counts that many times | 1 |
| change | 0 makes a viewer's first vote final | 1 |
| blind | 1 hides the bars until voting ends | 0 |
| color | purple, green, red, gold, cyan, pink | purple |
| pos | top or bottom of the browser source | top |
| lang | en or tr, the language of the words on the poll | the setup page's |
| simulate | 1 plays simulated polls, doesn't read chat and doesn't save | off |
| simplatform | twitch or kick: simulate only that platform | both |

## Raffle

A chat giveaway tool. The setup page is the tool itself: https://extensions.senchabot.com/setup/raffle (optional ?channel=NAME&platform=twitch or kick fills in the form).

- Pick Twitch or Kick and the channel. One raffle runs on one platform.
- Entry keyword: !join by default. A message counts when it is the keyword, or starts with it followed by a space. Case doesn't matter. Each person enters once.
- Known bots (for example Nightbot, StreamElements, Streamlabs, Moobot, Fossabot and Senchabot) can't enter. You can remove anyone with the x next to their name.
- Rules lock when the raffle starts. Reset All unlocks them.
- The winner is drawn from eligible entries with the browser's secure random number generator (crypto.getRandomValues).
- Settings, entries and winners are stored in the browser's localStorage, so a refresh keeps them. They stay in that browser only. Chat isn't read while the page is closed.

| Rule | Options | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subscribers Only | on, off (subscriber or founder badge; the broadcaster counts too) | off |
| Minimum Sub Months | 1 or more, only with Subscribers Only (read from the subscriber badge) | 1 |
| Max Wins Per Viewer | 1 to 5, or unlimited | 1 |
| Minimum Duration | 0 to 300 seconds before Draw Winner unlocks | 15 |

Winner overlay:
- URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/raffle-overlay, added as a 1920x1080 browser source. Optional parameters: preset (see Presets) and demo=1, which shows a sample winner on repeat.
- On Draw Winner the name appears in the middle of the screen, confetti bursts from both sides for 3 seconds, and the name disappears after 10 seconds.
- The winner reaches the overlay through the browser's BroadcastChannel, which only works inside one browser or app. A raffle page open in a separate browser such as Chrome can't reach an overlay inside OBS. Run the raffle page in the same app as the overlay and do a test draw before going live. The winner also always shows on the raffle page.

## OBS Bridge

Lets the people you authorize control OBS from Twitch or Kick chat.

- Setup page: https://extensions.senchabot.com/setup/obs-bridge. It builds a tool URL: https://extensions.senchabot.com/tools/obs-bridge?...
- Open the tool URL in a browser tab or an OBS Custom Browser Dock and keep it open while streaming. It is not a browser source. Closing it stops the commands.
- Needs obs-websocket 5, built into OBS Studio 28 and later. In OBS open Tools > WebSocket Server Settings, enable the WebSocket server and copy the password from Show Connect Info.
- The tool connects from the browser to OBS. If OBS is closed or the password is wrong, it tries again every 5 seconds.
- The tool page lists the OBS scenes. Pick Main and BRB there; the picks and user changes are saved in the page's URL. Copy Updated URL copies it (an OBS dock keeps opening the URL it was created with).
- Password: the OBS WebSocket password is saved in the tool URL (obsWebsocketPassword), and opening that URL loads the page from extensions.senchabot.com with the password in it. Treat the URL like a password: don't share it or show it on stream.

Commands (the whole message must be the command, case doesn't matter):

| Default command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| !scene NAME | Switches to the scene named NAME; if no exact match, the first scene whose name contains it |
| brb | Switches to the BRB scene |
| back | Switches to the Main scene |
| !startstream / !stopstream | Starts / stops the stream |
| !startrecord / !stoprecord | Starts / stops recording |

Only users on the authorized list can run commands. With an empty list nobody can, not even the broadcaster. Each user is tied to a platform, so the same name on the other platform can't use commands.

URL parameters:

| Parameter | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twitch | Twitch channel to listen to | none |
| kick | Kick channel to listen to | none |
| commandUser | comma list of platform:name, for example twitch:bob,kick:alice | none |
| obsWebsocketUrl | WebSocket address of OBS | ws://127.0.0.1:4455 |
| obsWebsocketPassword | OBS WebSocket password | none |
| mainScene | scene used by back | Main Scene |
| brbScene | scene used by brb | BRB Scene |
| cmdScene | command text | !scene |
| cmdBrb | command text | brb |
| cmdBack | command text | back |
| cmdStartStream | command text | !startstream |
| cmdStopStream | command text | !stopstream |
| cmdStartRecord | command text | !startrecord |
| cmdStopRecord | command text | !stoprecord |

## Spin Wheel

A chat-driven spinning wheel for game names, challenges or any list of choices. The setup page builds the overlay: https://extensions.senchabot.com/setup/spin-wheel, and the overlay runs at https://extensions.senchabot.com/widgets/spin-wheel. The quick manual tool still runs at https://extensions.senchabot.com/tools/spin-wheel.

- Type one option per line. The wheel updates as you type, up to 100 slices.
- Start a line with 2x, 3x, ... for extra slices: 2x Tetris wins twice as often.
- Viewers type !spin in Twitch or Kick chat to spin. Who may spin is a setting: everyone, subs only, or mods only (mods and the broadcaster can always spin).
- One global cooldown for the whole chat (30 seconds by default, 0 turns it off). While it runs, the overlay counts the wait down on screen and new !spin messages are skipped.
- Press Spin: the winner is picked with the browser's secure random number generator (crypto.getRandomValues) and lands with a live spinning animation, tick sounds, a victory jingle and confetti.
- Options, channels, permission and cooldown all live in the overlay URL. Paste it back on the setup page to edit it.
- No login: the overlay reads public chat anonymously.
- Spins on the tool page stay on that page; only !spin spins the overlay.
- With a preset, the wheel's rim, slices and labels, the winner card and the cooldown note take the preset's colors, fonts and frame.
- Two colors: the slices take turns between two colors instead of the full set, the classic orange and purple or the preset's accent and panel color. On by default with a preset. With an odd number of slices, the first and last share a color.
- URL parameters: twitch, kick, o (options joined with |), cd (cooldown seconds, 0-300, default 30), perm (all, subs, mods; default all), sound (1 or 0, default 1), colors (2 for the two-color wheel, all for every color; default 2 with a preset, all in the classic look), preset (see Presets; default classic, the gold wheel), lang.

## Presets

A preset gives several widgets the same look: frame, fonts and colors. Page: https://extensions.senchabot.com/presets

- Widgets that take one: Chat Box, Stream Alerts, Sub Goal, Follower Goal, Counter, Event List, End Credits, Viewer Queue, Top Supporters, Lower Thirds, Task List, Featured Message, Emote Combo, Bits & Kicks Goal, Now Playing, Subathon Timer, Chat Poll, the Raffle winner overlay, Stream Countdown, Socials, Spin Wheel and Stream Frames, whose frame art comes from the preset. Emote Wall and Sub Sprout keep their own art.
- URL parameter on those widgets: preset, one of rift, realm, flower, ancient, agent, defuse, blocks, pizza, storm, boost, airdrop, conquest, operator, banner, glitch. Missing or unknown means classic, each widget's own look, so URLs from before presets look the same.
- Built-in presets, most made for a game: Rift (League of Legends), Realm (World of Warcraft), Ancient (Dota 2), Agent (Valorant), Defuse (Counter-Strike 2), Blocks (Minecraft), Storm (Fortnite), Boost (Rocket League), Airdrop (PUBG), Banner (Mount & Blade and Kingdom Come: Deliverance), plus Glitch, Operator, Conquest, Flower and Pizza, made just for fun. They are fan-made styles from colors, free Google Fonts and original drawings, with no game art, and aren't affiliated with the game makers.
- A preset brings its own colors and fonts: with one set, the color parameters and Stream Alerts' theme are ignored. font (inter, roboto, nunito, mono, serif or system) draws the widget in that font instead of the preset's two, keeping the preset's colors, frame and effect (the Font box under the preset picker); Chat Box picks its fonts with its own font and userFont. Layout settings (Subathon style, Chat Box layout, poll position and so on) still apply.
- Every built-in preset also has an effect of its own, played on bars as they grow, on panels as they come in, now and then while idle, and bigger when a goal is reached: Rift (teal energy and a rune flash), Realm (golden light shafts and stars), Flower (little flowers and pink petals floating around bars, a cherry blossom opening at a bar's edge as it grows), Ancient (smoldering bars and rising embers), Agent (a blade slash and shards), Defuse (an amber scan and a blinking red light), Blocks (blocks popping in), Pizza (pizza slices floating around bars, a slice popping out as a bar grows, a whole pizza for a reached goal), Storm (a blueprint grid that turns solid, lightning on a win), Boost (speed lines, flames and a shockwave), Airdrop (flare smoke and landing dust), Conquest (a capture sweep and radar pings), Operator (hit marks), Banner (bars hammered white-hot, throwing sparks, cooling to iron) and Glitch (panels tear and flicker like a broken signal). fx=0 turns a preset's effect off (the Effects switch under the preset picker); Stream Countdown and Stream Frames with motion=0, and Chat Box with animation=none, keep it off too.
- The presets page can set a default preset that every setup page in that browser starts with. A setup page opened with ?preset= in its link starts on that preset instead: the presets page links that way, and so do the home page previews, which show a random preset on every visit. A dice beside the preset picker picks a random preset. Widgets already in OBS keep their look until they get a new URL; the presets page takes pasted widget URLs and gives them back with the preset added.
- Community presets are JSON files in the source repository (apps/extensions/src/features/presets/community), added by pull request.

## FAQ

Q: Is Senchabot Extensions free?
A: Yes. All thirteen widgets and tools are free: Chat Box, Emote Wall, Sub Sprout, Subathon Timer, Stream Alerts, Sub Goal, Stream Frames, Stream Countdown, Chat Poll, Socials, Raffle, OBS Bridge and Spin Wheel. There's no paid plan, watermark or premium account. The source code is open on GitHub under the GPL-3.0 license.

Q: What does "no login required" mean?
A: You don't create an account on the site, you don't log in with Twitch or Kick, and you don't download anything. You type your channel name and the setup page gives you a URL. The widgets read public chat anonymously, so they can't post in chat, moderate, or access private info on your account.

Q: Is Senchabot Extensions affiliated with Twitch or Kick?
A: No. It is made by Senchabot, an open source community bot for Twitch, Discord, Kick and YouTube, and has no official connection to, partnership with or endorsement from Twitch or Kick.

Q: Which streaming software does it work with?
A: OBS Studio and any other streaming software that supports a browser source. Each widget runs as a web URL that you paste into the source.

Q: Which widgets support Twitch and which support Kick?
A: All thirteen support both. Chat Box, Emote Wall, Sub Sprout, Subathon Timer, Stream Alerts, Sub Goal, Counter and Chat Poll listen to a Twitch and a Kick channel in one URL. Spin Wheel does too. OBS Bridge listens for commands from both chats. Raffle runs on one platform at a time. Stream Frames and Socials read no chat. In Chat Box, 7TV emotes show on both platforms, BTTV and FFZ emotes on Twitch only.

Q: How do I change a widget later?
A: Change the settings on the setup page, copy the new URL and paste it over the old one in OBS. With Chat Box, Emote Wall, Sub Sprout, Subathon Timer, Stream Alerts, Sub Goal, Counter, Chat Poll and Spin Wheel you can paste your old URL into the Widget URL field on the setup page to get all your settings back.

Q: Will my old widget URLs keep working?
A: Yes. Parameter names, values and defaults stay the same. For example the old keep=true in Chat Box still means Forever, and Sub Sprout still reads the old channel and platform parameters.

Q: Where are my settings stored, and where does my data go?
A: Settings live in the widget URL, not in an account. Chat is read from Twitch and Kick, emotes come from 7TV, BetterTTV and FrankerFaceZ, and Twitch channel info from ivr.fi. Raffle entries and winners stay in your own browser. The OBS Bridge URL contains your OBS WebSocket password, so treat it like a password.

Q: Why does my widget look empty in OBS?
A: Chat Box and Emote Wall stay empty until something happens in chat, so send a message first. If there's still nothing, check that you typed just the channel name, not a link, and that it's spelled right.

Q: Is my OBS WebSocket password safe?
A: The connection to OBS goes straight from your browser to OBS. The password is saved in the tool URL, and opening that URL loads the page from extensions.senchabot.com with the password in it. Treat the link like a password.

Q: Does Chat Box restream to both platforms?
A: No. It only reads chat and shows it. Streaming to Twitch and Kick at once needs a separate multistreaming setup.

Q: How do I request a widget or report a bug?
A: Open an issue at https://github.com/senchabot-opensource/monorepo/issues/new. Include the widget URL (remove any password), your streaming software and what you see. Ideas also go to GitHub Discussions or the Senchabot Discord.
